Resolves #18740

`#16553` closed with one row deferred as *"a policy question for both repositories, not a regex fix"*: the published guard rejects the legacy `ticket-ref-ok` marker while the engine guard honours it. That had no teeth while CI ran 0.1.4. The 0.1.5 bump gave it teeth, and [neo-agent-skills#72](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/pull/72) shipped the missing form in 0.1.6. This is the engine half.

## Deltas

**The deadlock, measured — one comment, four repairs, both implementations run directly:**

| repair | engine (pre-commit) | published (CI) |
|---|---|---|
| keep `ticket-ref-ok` | green | **RED** |
| migrate to the typed marker | **RED** | **RED** |
| remove the marker, keep `@see #11133` | **RED** | **RED** |
| delete the reference itself | green | green |

The documented migration was the worst option, and the only both-green state deletes the provenance the comment exists to carry.

**`buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs`** — `withEscapedRefsRemoved` mirrors `withEscapedColorsRemoved`: it blanks the annotated token rather than skipping the line, so a second unannotated ref sharing that line stays visible. `css-color` is excluded from the ref form, so a colour marker still cannot relabel a short ticket. `REF_ESCAPE_PATTERN` is copied from 0.1.6 rather than paraphrased, for the reason the file already gives — the only thing this buys is the two agreeing.

**The bare marker retires, and this file's own comment is the authority for that.** It read:

> Rejecting the bare form here would block at pre-commit every deliberate ref that has no typed equivalent upstream, which is a policy question rather than a lint repair.

0.1.6 is that equivalent, so the condition the exception rested on is gone, and honouring a marker CI rejects is now itself the divergence. Retiring it also removes a real defect independent of the divergence: `line.includes(ESCAPE_MARKER)` was a **whole-line bypass**, which is exactly what the typed escape was scoped to avoid.

**Seven comments migrated.** Three carried a bare marker on a real ref; four more carried a marker escaping nothing at all — invisible to this guard, `invalid-escape` to the published one, and vestigial after the retirement.

**The migration shape is load-bearing and was verified against both guards rather than assumed.** The marker binds to the token it follows, so the ref goes first and the marker sits adjacent — and it must **close on that same line**, because both implementations read a comment row at a time. My first attempt split all three across lines and both rejected all three, agreeing on the failure. That agreement is the property this ticket buys.

**Three pins to 0.1.6** — devDependency, lockfile, and the `uses:` SHA to `@6b009521`. Fewer than three leaves two jobs judging this repository by different releases: `npx --no-install` resolves from the lockfile, while archaeology, substrate size and PR body install `@${SKILLS_VERSION}` into `runner.temp`.

published  --base origin/dev  →  8 file(s),      0 violations   exit 0

Eight files, not zero — the earlier run of this pair reported `0 files in scope` because nothing was committed yet, which is a green over an empty population and says nothing.

## Test Evidence

`npm run test-unit` → **4101 passed, 2 skipped, exit 0**.

Guard spec: 26 arms, three flipped and five added, red-first against the pre-change implementation (2 failed / 24 passed before, 26 after).

**The flipped arm is worth reading before approving.** It asserted:

> *an unrecognised kind is NOT a bypass — accepting it here would pass the hook and fail CI, the same divergence reversed*

Its **reasoning was right and its premise moved**. Rejecting a free-reason marker was the safe side only while upstream had no typed equivalent for a deliberate ref. Upstream now accepts one, so rejecting it here *is* the divergence that arm was defending against. The comment saying so sits beside it.

**Measured before removing the row-level skip, not after:** disabling it and running the full audit reported **5 violations across 1120 files** — three bare markers on a ref, and two carrying no marker at all.

## Post-Merge Validation

- **Two pre-existing full-audit violations are out of scope and are latent landmines**: `test/playwright/unit/app/content/CrossLinkIssuesUrl.spec.mjs:22` and `test/playwright/unit/grid/PoolingRuntimeUpdates.spec.mjs:5` carry bare refs with no marker. They violate today, independent of this change. CI never sees them because `ticket-archaeology-lint.yml` runs `--base origin/dev` — changed files only — and nobody has touched those two. The first PR that edits either will red on prose it did not write.
- `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` still pins `@27e151d9` (0.1.5) and its lockfile resolves 0.1.5. Same three-pin move, not folded in here.
- `neomjs/devindex` remains on `@72965ba5`, a coordinate predating `SKILLS_VERSION` entirely — a different shape needing its own read.
- A reference **inside** the marker's reason text, and `NAMED_TRACKING_PATTERNS` prose carrying no `#` (`pull request 11982`, `ADR 0004 §2.2`), stay out of reach of token binding in both implementations. Recorded rather than widened: swallowing them is the row-level escape hatch this change just removed.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: `ESCAPE_MARKER` stays exported while its only remaining use is the error string that announces its own retirement. I checked for external consumers and found none — the `ESCAPE_MARKER` hits in `buildScripts/util/check-derived-domain.mjs` are that guard's own unrelated `'derived-domain-ok:'`. Keeping the constant so the message can name the retired form is right; keeping it **exported** is surface that now has no reader. Non-blocking, and I am not asking for it in this PR — a retired name is exactly the thing a later sweep should remove once nothing cites it.

**What I verified rather than accepted:**

**Cross-guard agreement — the property #16553's AC-2 exists to protect.** I ran the engine guard from this branch against the published 0.1.6 guard fetched from the pinned SHA, nine cases spanning the whole escape family:

```
agreement: 9/9
```

Typed marker on a ref, marker through a closing paren, empty reason, the legacy bare marker, a bare ref, `css-color` refusing to relabel, the colour escape still binding, an HTML entity, and a second unexcused ref sharing the row — the two implementations return the same verdict on every one. The divergence is closed, not narrowed.

**The pattern is copied, not paraphrased — character-identical:**

```
engine     REF_ESCAPE_PATTERN = /#(\d+)['"`)\]]{0,3}\s*\[not-ticket-ref:(?!\s*css-color\s*\])\s*[^\]\s][^\]]*\]/g
published  REF_ESCAPE_RE      = /#(\d+)['"`)\]]{0,3}\s*\[not-ticket-ref:(?!\s*css-color\s*\])\s*[^\]\s][^\]]*\]/g
```

Only the binding name differs. That includes the `\s*[^\]\s]` non-blank-reason tightening I raised as RA-1 on `neo-agent-skills#72`, so the engine inherits the fix rather than an earlier draft of it.

**All three pins, and the third one checked at its target — this is the trap that red-ed #18734 today.** Bumping the dependency without moving `uses: …@<sha>` leaves the baseline job installing the previous release and flagging the exact lines the release exists to pass:

| pin | value |
|---|---|
| devDependency | `0.1.6` |
| `uses:` SHA | `@6b009521…` |
| **that SHA's `SKILLS_VERSION`** | **`0.1.6` ×3** — counted at the target, not assumed from the bump |

`neo-agent-skills@0.1.6` is live on the registry, so the pin resolves.

**The bypass is gone, the name is not.** `line.includes(ESCAPE_MARKER)` — a whole-line escape, the thing the typed form was scoped to avoid — no longer exists. The constant survives only so the error can tell an author *why* their marker stopped working, which is the right trade.

**Migrations.** Zero `ticket-ref-ok` occurrences remain in any touched file; three gained a typed marker on a real reference, the vestigial ones were removed outright rather than translated.
